facts.statement: Lonchidion is an extinct genus of shark belonging to the family Lonchidiidae.
facts.quote: Lonchidion is a genus of extinct hybodont in the family Lonchidiidae.

facts.statement: The genus Lonchidion was first described by Richard Estes in 1964, with L. selachas as the type species.
facts.quote: Lonchidion was first described by Richard Estes in 1964, and the type species is L. selachas.

facts.statement: Lonchidion fossils range from the Middle Triassic (Ladinian) to the very end of the Cretaceous (Maastrichtian).
facts.quote: The genus first appears in the fossil record during the Middle Triassic (Ladinian) and was among the last surviving hybodont genera, with its youngest known fossils dating to the very end of the Cretaceous (Maastrichtian).

facts.statement: Fossils of Lonchidion have been discovered worldwide.
facts.quote: Fossils of Lonchidion have been found worldwide.

facts.statement: Lonchidion is thought to be euryhaline, as fossils are frequently found in freshwater and brackish deposits.
facts.quote: The genus has been proposed to be euryhaline, and is often found in freshwater and brackish deposits.

facts.statement: A preserved specimen of Lonchidion is among the smallest known elasmobranchs, measuring around 3.5 cm in length.
facts.quote: This specimen is among the smallest known elasmobranchs, at around 3.5 cm in length.

facts.statement: Lonchidion had low-crowned teeth likely adapted for grinding hard prey through durophagy.
facts.quote: The teeth of the genus are low crowned, and probably served to grind hard prey (durophagy).

facts.statement: Some authors debate the validity of Lonchidion as a genus, suggesting its teeth represent a juvenile morphological type lost in adults rather than a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Some authors have proposed that Lonchidion is not a valid genus, and that its teeth instead represent a morphological type present among many juvenile hybodonts but that is later lost in adults.

facts.statement: Lonchidion is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for Lonchidion spans from the Carnian to the Maastrichtian, approximately 237 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Maastrichtian (237 to 66 million years ago)
